questions.text: Choose the one word which can be substituted for the given group of words: **"A person who speaks many languages"**.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use etymology/root words. 'Poly-' means many (polygon), '-glot' means tongue/language (glottis). 'Linguist' studies language structure; 'Grammarian' studies grammar; 'Orator' is a public speaker. Only 'Polyglot' implies speaking multiple languages. Full Solution: A Polyglot is a person with a command of many languages. A Linguist is an expert in linguistics (scientific study of language), not necessarily a speaker of many languages.

questions.text: Starting from point X, Ravi walks 10 m north, turns right and walks 15 m, then turns left and walks 10 m. In which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Plot movements on a grid – north 10, east 15, north 10 gives a net displacement of 20 m north and 15 m east, i.e. North‑East. Step‑by‑step: After first move coordinates (0,10); right turn adds (15,0) → (15,10); left turn adds (0,10) → (15,20); the resultant vector lies in the North‑East quadrant, which is option D.

questions.text: ‘Doctor’ is related to ‘Hospital’ in the same way as ‘Teacher’ is related to ______.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognise the pattern ‘Profession : Workplace’. Doctor works in a Hospital, so Teacher works in a School. Full solution: The first pair shows a professional and their typical place of work. Applying the same relation, a teacher’s workplace is a school; student, book, and classroom are not the primary workplace. Hence the answer is School.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom **"To cry wolf"**.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate literal interpretations of 'cry' and 'wolf' (Options A, C). The idiom originates from Aesop's fable where a shepherd boy repeatedly tricks villagers; thus, it means raising a false alarm. Option B fits perfectly. Full Solution: 'To cry wolf' means to claim that something is happening when it is not, with the result that subsequent genuine claims are disbelieved. It signifies giving a false alarm.

questions.text: A motorboat goes 10 km upstream and returns back to the starting point in 55 minutes. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, find the speed of the motorboat in still water.
questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Verification): Convert 55 min to 11/12 hr. Check options for total time = 10/(x-2) + 10/(x+2). For 20 km/h: 10/18 + 10/22 ≈ 1.00 hr (60 min) > 55 min. For 22 km/h: 10/20 + 10/24 = 0.5 + 0.4167 = 0.9167 hr = 55 min. Correct. Full Solution: Let speed in still water = x km/h. Upstream speed = (x-2), Downstream = (x+2). Total time = 10/(x-2) + 10/(x+2) = 55/60 = 11/12. => 20x/(x^2-4) = 11/12 => 240x = 11x^2 - 44 => 11x^2 - 240x - 44 = 0 => 11x^2 - 242x + 2x - 44 = 0 => 11x(x-22) + 2(x-22) = 0 => (x-22)(11x+2)=0 => x = 22 km/h.

questions.text: Under which land revenue settlement system, introduced by the British, was the settlement made directly with the cultivator (ryot) recognizing him as the proprietor of the land, subject to the payment of land revenue?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ryotwari -> 'Ryot' means cultivator/peasant. Direct settlement with Ryot. Zamindari -> Settlement with Zamindar (intermediary). Mahalwari -> Settlement with Mahal (village/estate) collectively. Full Solution: The Ryotwari system, introduced by Thomas Munro in Madras and later extended to Bombay, made the cultivator the proprietor of land with direct responsibility to pay revenue to the state. The Permanent Settlement (Bengal) created Zamindars as proprietors. The Mahalwari system (North-West Provinces) made the village community jointly responsible.

questions.text: In the context of the Indian Economy, which of the following components is included in M1 (Narrow Money) but NOT in M0 (Reserve Money / High Powered Money)?

options.label: C
options.text: Cash Reserves of Commercial Banks with RBI

questions.solution: Shortcut: M0 (Monetary Base) = Central Bank Liabilities (Currency in Circulation + Bankers' Deposits + Other Deposits). M1 = Currency with Public + Demand Deposits + Other Deposits with RBI. 'Demand Deposits' are Commercial Bank liabilities, created by money multiplier, not part of RBI's balance sheet liabilities (M0). Detailed Solution: M0 (Reserve Money) consists of Currency in Circulation, Bankers' Deposits with RBI, and Other Deposits with RBI. M1 (Narrow Money) consists of Currency with Public, Demand Deposits with Commercial Banks (Current/Savings), and Other Deposits with RBI. Demand Deposits are liabilities of commercial banks, whereas M0 represents the monetary liabilities of the Central Bank (RBI).

questions.text: The Chauri Chaura incident (February 1922), where protesters set fire to a police station killing 22 policemen, led Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw which nationwide movement?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate 'Chauri Chaura' (1922) with the 'Non-Cooperation Movement' (1920-22). Civil Disobedience started in 1930 (Dandi March); Quit India was 1942. Full Solution: Then on-cooperation Movement (1920-22) was the first mass movement led by Gandhi. Following the violent clash at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP) on 5 February 1922, Gandhi, adhering strictly ton on-violence, called off the movement unilaterally on 12 February 1922, much to the dismay of other leaders.

Shortcut: For any \(n \ge 5\), \(n!\) ends in 0, so \((n!)^n\) ends in 0. Only the first four terms contribute to the unit digit. \(1^1=1\), \(2^2=4\), \(6^3\rightarrow 6\), \(24^4\rightarrow 4^4=256\rightarrow 6\). Sum of unit digits = \(1+4+6+6=17\). Unit digit is 7. Full Solution: \(5!=120\) (ends in 0), hence all higher factorials end in 0. Calculating unit digits: \(1^1=1\), \(2^2=4\), \(3!=6 \Rightarrow 6^3=216 \Rightarrow 6\), \(4!=24 \Rightarrow 4^4=256 \Rightarrow 6\). Total unit digit = \(1+4+6+6=17 \equiv 7\).

questions.text: Which committee recommended the establishment of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in India to decide the policy repo rate?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Map committees to their key recommendations. Urjit Patel Committee (2014) -> MPC & Inflation Targeting. Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) -> Small Finance Banks / Payment Banks. Bimal Jalan Committee (various) -> Capital Account Convertibility / RBI Economic Capital Framework. Raghuram Rajan Committee (2008) -> Financial Sector Reforms. Worked Solution: The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 was amended in 2016 to provide a statutory basis for the MPC based on the recommendations of the Urjit Patel Committee (Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework, 2014).

questions.text: A vessel contains 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres of milk is taken out and replaced with water. This process is repeated two more times. What is the final quantity of milk in the vessel?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use replacement formula: Final Amount = Initial \(\times (1 - \frac{\text{Replaced}}{\text{Total}})^n\). Here Initial = 80, Replaced = 8, Total = 80, n = 3. Fraction = 1/10. Milk left = \(80 \times (9/10)^3 = 80 \times 729/1000 = 58.32\) litres. Full: 1st replacement: Milk = 72 L. 2nd replacement: Milk removed = \(8 \times (72/80) = 7.2\); Milk left = 64.8 L. 3rd replacement: Milk removed = \(8 \times (64.8/80) = 6.48\); Milk left = 64.8 - 6.48 = 58.32 L.

questions.text: Rohan walks 10 metres North, then turns left and walks 5 metres. He then turns left again and walks 10 metres. Finally, he turns right and walks 7 metres. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track Net Displacement. North 10m cancels South 10m (3rd leg). Net Vertical = 0. Horizontal: 1st Left (West) 5m + Final Right (West) 7m = 12m West. Distance = 12m. Step-by-step: Start at Origin (0,0). 1. North 10m -> (0, 10). 2. Left (West) 5m -> (-5, 10). 3. Left (South) 10m -> (-5, 0). 4. Right (West) 7m -> (-12, 0). Final coordinate (-12, 0). Distance from origin = sqrt((-12)^2 + 0^2) = 12 metres.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Find the differences between consecutive terms: 4, 6, 8, 10. The differences increase by 2 each time. Next difference = 12. Add to last term: 30 + 12 = 42. Full Solution: The series follows the pattern n(n+1) i.e., 1×2=2, 2×3=6, 3×4=12, 4×5=20, 5×6=30. The next term corresponds to n=6: 6×7=42. Alternatively, the first-level differences form an arithmetic progression (4, 6, 8, 10) with a common difference of 2, making the next difference 12. 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.text: Change the following sentence into Passive Voice: "They are building a new bridge across the river."

options.label: A
options.text: A new bridge is being built across the river by them.

options.label: B
options.text: A new bridge has been built across the river by them.

options.label: C
options.text: A new bridge was being built across the river by them.

options.label: D
options.text: A new bridge is built across the river by them.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the tense as Present Continuous Active ('are building'). The Passive structure for this tense is 'is/am/are + being + V3'. Only Option A follows this rule. Full Solution: The object 'a new bridge' becomes the subject. The verb 'are building' changes to 'is being built' (singular verb for singular subject). The original subject 'They' becomes the agent 'by them'.

questions.text: Find the unit digit of the expression \((6^{25} \times 4^{18}) + (3^{41} \times 5^{12})\).
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits. \(6^n\) always ends in 6. \(4^{\text{even}}\) ends in 6. First product unit digit = \(6 \times 6 = 36 \rightarrow 6\). \(3^{41}\): cyclicity 4, remainder 1 \(\rightarrow 3\). \(5^n\) always ends in 5. Second product unit digit = \(3 \times 5 = 15 \rightarrow 5\). Sum of unit digits = \(6 + 5 = 11 \rightarrow 1\). Full: Cyclicity of 6 is 1 (always 6). Cyclicity of 4 is 2 (4, 6); 18 is even \(\rightarrow 6\). First part unit digit = 6. Cyclicity of 3 is 4 (3, 9, 7, 1); \(41 \bmod 4 = 1 \rightarrow 3\). Cyclicity of 5 is 1 (always 5). Second part unit digit = 5. Final unit digit = 6 + 5 = 11 \(\rightarrow 1\).
